games.2026_02_DET_BUF: Played Thursday: Buffalo 41, Detroit 31. The pick was Bills at 65 percent with a blended margin of 4.7; the actual margin was 10. Detroit's three missing linemen showed up as expected, and the numbers here are frozen at what was published before kickoff.
games.2026_02_CAR_ATL: Two depleted rosters and the closest game on the slate, now leaning Carolina by a hair after Friday's report. Atlanta named Cooper Rush the starter with Penix out and Tua doubtful, Da'Shawn Hand is done for the year, Jalon Walker is on IR, James Pearce Jr. is suspended, and A.J. Terrell and Chris Lindstrom are questionable. Carolina is missing both starting tackles through Week 4, Nic Scourton for the season, and Bobby Brown III this week, and its defense just allowed 59 points. The model's own margin is Falcons by one and a half; the market has Carolina by 2.5, and the blend lands on Carolina by less than half a point.
games.2026_02_CIN_HOU: Houston rated well above Cincinnati entering the season, but Friday's report gutted the Texans: Nico Collins is out with a hamstring, Jadeveon Clowney and guard Ed Ingram are out, and linebackers To'oTo'o (IR), Hummel and Speed are all gone. Cincinnati is the healthiest team on the slate apart from Joe Burrow's questionable tag for back tightness, which he says is nothing (full practice Friday, modeled as 85 percent to start). The roof will be closed. The model has Houston by under two; the market moved to 2.5, and the blend makes the Texans a slim Lean.
games.2026_02_CLE_TB: Tampa Bay rated five and a half points better than Cleveland before the season and the gap widened after the Browns' 34-10 loss in Jacksonville. Todd Monken kept Deshaun Watson as the starter despite a poor debut. Both teams are relatively healthy for this one, so the number is about ratings and weather: 89 degrees with a 70 percent thunderstorm chance compresses the margin slightly. The model has the Bucs by six, the market by 8.5, and the blend by about seven.
games.2026_02_GB_NYJ: Green Bay's rating fell more than a point after the loss in Minnesota and the Packers are still without Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs, with two starting linemen questionable. But the Jets are worse off: their rating is the lowest on the slate, Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin, two to three weeks) and first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle, week to week) are both out, and Joseph Ossai is out. The model makes Green Bay a six-point road favorite; the market shortened to 3.5 during the week.
games.2026_02_MIN_CHI: The biggest model-versus-market gap of the week. Chicago's rating rose after the 59-point outburst in Carolina, but the Bears have Ozzy Trapilo and Tyrique Stevenson questionable and three defenders on PUP. Minnesota now goes to Carson Wentz with Kyler Murray ruled out, has lost running back Jordan Mason to IR and Jauan Jennings for the week, and Brian O'Neill is questionable. The data alone has the Bears by about two; the market has 4.5, and the blend settles on three and a half.
games.2026_02_NO_BAL: Baltimore's 41-23 win in Indianapolis was the best opponent-adjusted performance of Week 1, but the Ravens are banged up for the home opener: Nnamdi Madubuike is out, Zay Flowers is doubtful, and Ronnie Stanley, Trey Hendrickson and John Simpson are questionable. New Orleans gets Alvin Kamara and Cameron Jordan back, though Chris Olave is questionable with a hamstring. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson remains on IR. Model and market both still make it Ravens by about eight, down from nine at midweek.
games.2026_02_PHI_TEN: Philadelphia's rating fell after the narrow win over Washington, the Eagles lost Landon Dickerson to IR, Jonathan Greenard was ruled out again, and Andrew Mukuba is questionable. Tennessee's rating dropped too after the loss to the Jets, with Cedric Gray and Cordale Flott questionable. The model has the Eagles by under five on the road, the market by seven; the blend is six, which keeps Philadelphia a Moderate pick rather than a High one.
games.2026_02_PIT_NE: New England's rating takes a big injury hit: A.J. Brown is on IR with a high-ankle sprain, Harold Landry is on PUP, and Carlton Davis, Dre'Mont Jones and center Ben Brown are questionable. TreVeyon Henderson is not on the report and will make his debut. Pittsburgh ruled out Joey Porter Jr. and has Michael Pittman and Troy Fautanu questionable. The model likes the Patriots at home by about four; the market's 5.5 looks generous, and the blend is 4.8.
games.2026_02_JAX_DEN: The one game where the data and the market pick different teams. Jacksonville's rout of Cleveland made it the second-highest-rated team in the league, and Denver's 31-10 loss in Kansas City, with Jonathon Cooper still on the exempt list, dropped the Broncos below average. Denver also listed running back RJ Harvey and receiver Marvin Mims as non-participants Wednesday. On the data alone the Jaguars are five-and-a-half-point road favorites; the market has Denver by 2.5. The blend gives Jacksonville the narrowest of edges, so this is a coin flip either way.
games.2026_02_LV_LAC: The Chargers rated as a slight favorite before the season, but the offensive line is without Tyler Biadasz and now Trey Pipkins, Elijah Molden is out, Denzel Perryman is on IR, and Ladd McConkey is questionable with the rib injury. Las Vegas gets the Kirk Cousins upgrade over last year's quarterback play, but center Jackson Powers-Johnson and Darien Porter are out and Brock Bowers is doubtful. The model has Los Angeles by about three; the market says 6.5, and the blend is about five.
games.2026_02_MIA_SF: The largest gap on the slate. San Francisco came out of Melbourne healthy: Friday's report carries no designation for Kittle, Bosa or McCaffrey, which also puts to rest a midweek aggregator claim that McCaffrey had gone to IR. Miami is a bottom-three team by rating with a first-year starter at quarterback, Kenneth Grant on IR and edge Chop Robinson out. The model has the 49ers by twelve, the market by 13.5, and the simulation gives Miami roughly one chance in six.
games.2026_02_SEA_ARI: Seattle is the top-rated team in the model but Sam Darnold has been officially ruled out with a glute strain (no surgery, possibly back in Week 3). Drew Lock, who finished the comeback against New England, costs the Seahawks about two and a half points, and Nick Emmanwori remains questionable. Arizona is short James Conner and has two starters questionable, but its rating jumped after the upset in Los Angeles. Roof closed. The model has Seattle by five and a half; the market shortened from 4.5 to 3.5 once Darnold was ruled out.
games.2026_02_WAS_DAL: Two below-average teams getting worse. Dallas lost Tyler Smith to IR and ruled out Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown; Washington is without Laremy Tunsil, Johnny Newton and Trey Amos, and Frankie Luvu and Chig Okonkwo were ruled out Friday. Jayden Daniels grades as a modest upgrade on last year's Commanders quarterback play. Roof closed. The market settled back to Cowboys by 3.5; the model has three, and the blend is about three and a half.
games.2026_02_IND_KC: Kansas City's rating climbed after the Monday-night win and Mahomes came through his return healthy, but left tackle Josh Simmons and safety Chamarri Conner are out and Chris Jones is questionable with the calf he played through in Week 1. Indianapolis dropped more than three points after being routed at home by Baltimore and is close to full strength. The weather is the wild card: a 70 percent rain chance and 15 mph wind at Arrowhead pull the margin and the total down. The model has the Chiefs by five, the market by six.
games.2026_02_NYG_LA: The Rams fell three points in the ratings after the loss in Melbourne and then lost Myles Garrett to IR until at least Week 6. Aaron Donald makes his season debut Monday, but Puka Nacua was added to the report Friday with a hip issue and did not practice. New York's Jaxson Dart played well in Dallas and Malik Nabers is back. Los Angeles gets extra rest after its Thursday game in Australia. The model has the Rams by five, the market by seven, and the blend by six.
